figs/678622126e789bb5.jpg: **The global UMAP of all spots separates by Leiden cluster, and several clusters are dominated by single sections.** Each point is a Visium spot from all 10 sections, on a UMAP built from PCA of log-normalised expression (no HVG selection, no batch correction). figs/81a622f6c6a739e8.jpg: **On the global UMAP, manual region labels match expression clusters only partly, and many spots are unlabelled.** Each point is a Visium spot on the same UMAP as §3, coloured by the hand-drawn region annotation; grey is NA (no label, about 8,050 of 25,660 spots). figs/06b9dd28038883d6.jpg: **The ten cluster-derived 'regions' are mapped onto every section, including the WT and P24215 sections.** Each panel is one section (treatment in brackets) with spots coloured by `re_annotation_regions`, the hand mapping of the 13 Leiden-0.3 clusters to ten brain regions. Colours are assigned per panel from the regions present in that section, so the same colour can mean different regions in different panels (for example olive is Ventricular area in some panels and Thalamus in others); read each panel's own legend.
figs/078676c04ab50737.jpg: **Top marker genes for each of the 13 Leiden-0.3 clusters, used to name the regions.** Each panel is one cluster against all other spots (t-test). Genes are ranked on x, and y is the test score. The markers fit the region names in §8: cluster 0 Ppp1r1b/Penk (striatum), 4 Plp1/Mbp/Mobp (corpus callosum), 6 Nnat/Pmch (hypothalamus), 10 Prkcd/Adarb1 (thalamus), 11 Ppp1r1b/Arpp21 (striatum) and 12 Ttr/Enpp2 (choroid plexus, the 'Ventricular area').
figs/07e19ab3a4c970e8.jpg: **In the WT section, PIG and OLIG module scores by Leiden-0.75 cluster.** Each row is a Leiden-0.75 cluster (WT spots only). The two columns are the plaque-induced gene (PIG, 52-gene list) score and the oligodendrocyte (OLIG) score. Colour is the mean score scaled 0–1 per column and dot size is the fraction of spots with a positive score; the dendrogram groups clusters by these two scores. Even in WT, the PIG score is highest in a few clusters (for example 15, 9 and 4) and OLIG peaks in clusters 10 and 17. Scaling is within this WT subset, so colours cannot be compared with the BRICHOS panel.
figs/5e1d81b2640f4ca2.jpg: **H&E images of the ten sections with no spots overlaid.** Each panel is one section (treatment in brackets), drawn with `color=None` to show the tissue only. The sections differ in cutting plane and in how much hippocampus, ventricle and ventral tissue they include, which matters for region-wise comparisons. The P24215 sections (WT 101 and BRICHOS 201 and 301) are stained paler than the P28052 sections. P28052_201 has a round artefact near the bottom of the capture area.
figs/718ea8990563c401.jpg: **Region composition differs between treatment groups, with WT richer in hypothalamus, hippocampus and thalamus spots.** Each stacked bar is a treatment group, and segments are the fraction of its spots in each cluster-derived region. WT (one section) has visibly larger hypothalamus, hippocampal formation and thalamus fractions and a smaller caudoputamen fraction than PBS or BRICHOS. These composition differences reflect how each section was cut, and they feed any whole-section comparison.
figs/854ab23090deeedc.jpg: **Top marker genes for each of the 23 Leiden-0.75 clusters.** Each panel is one cluster against all other spots (Wilcoxon test). Genes are ranked on x, and y is the test score. The markers are anatomically coherent: cluster 1 striatal (Rasd2, Ppp1r1b, Drd2), 9 astrocyte/Apoe (Slc1a2, Apoe, Cst3, Clu, Gfap), 10 oligodendrocyte (Mbp, Plp1, Mobp), 12 hypothalamic (Ndrg2, Pmch) and 13/14 thalamic (Prkcd, Tcf7l2, Slc17a6). Cluster 21 has very low scores (top score about 4), so it is weakly defined.
figs/9deb5ea001eb9892.jpg: **The PIG score is high in PBS and BRICHOS spots and low in WT spots.** Rows are treatment groups (all spots). Columns are the PIG (52-gene) and OLIG module scores. Colour is the mean score scaled 0–1 per column and dot size is the fraction of spots with a positive score. PBS has the highest scaled PIG score, BRICHOS is slightly lower and WT is lowest. figs/c8d91848d78f079f.jpg: **In BRICHOS sections, PIG and OLIG module scores by Leiden-0.75 cluster.** Each row is a Leiden-0.75 cluster (BRICHOS spots only). The PIG score is highest in clusters 10, 9, 12 and 20, and OLIG in 10 and 17 (oligodendrocyte clusters). This is the BRICHOS counterpart of the WT panel; scaling is within each subset, so colours are not comparable between panels.
figs/d89ca98a3a90bf04.jpg: **Leiden clusterings at nine resolutions on the global UMAP.** Each panel is the same UMAP of all spots, coloured by Leiden clusters at resolutions 0.1 to 2.5, with cluster numbers on the data. Coarse resolutions give a few large clusters; 2.5 gives more than 50. Resolution 0.3 (13 clusters) was chosen for the region mapping and 0.75 (23 clusters) for the module scoring.
figs/dd7501f6880397c4.jpg: **The 13 Leiden-0.3 clusters form anatomical bands in every section.** Each panel is one section (treatment in brackets) with spots coloured by Leiden-0.3 cluster. Clusters 1 and 2 form the outer and inner cortical layers in every section, and cluster 0 fills the striatum. Clusters such as 6, 9, 10 and 11 appear only in some sections (for example the P28052_102 and 103 sections, which include thalamus and hypothalamus). This is the clustering hand-mapped to the ten regions used in later regional analyses.
figs/21ce4ecf60a53aa1.jpg: **Six genes reported in Chen et al. 2020 by treatment group.** Rows are treatment groups (all spots). Columns are Cst7, Cd68, C1qa, Slc1a3, Clu and Mbp. Colour is mean expression scaled 0–1 per gene and dot size is the fraction of spots expressing the gene. Cst7, Cd68 and C1qa are almost absent or low in WT and high in both PBS and BRICHOS, matching the published direction. Slc1a3 is highest in WT. No statistics were computed.
figs/c7501be38f5e1386.jpg: **Itm2b/Itm2c and four tight-junction genes by treatment group.** Rows are treatment groups (all spots) and columns are Itm2b, Itm2c, Cldn5, Ocln, F11r and Tjp1. Colour is mean expression scaled 0–1 per gene across the three groups, and dot size is the fraction of spots expressing it. Because of the per-gene scaling, small absolute differences look large: Itm2c is unchanged in the spot-level tests (|log2FC| < 0.02, §12), and the tight-junction shifts are all below 0.4 log2FC. Cldn5 is highest in WT, and F11r, Ocln and Tjp1 are highest in PBS.
figs/0107c297d95286b0.jpg: **Endocytosis-related GO terms among genes lower in PBS than WT.** Each bubble is a GO Biological Process term from g:Profiler over-representation analysis of genes down in PBS vs WT (spot-level t-test, FDR ≤ 0.05, log2FC ≤ −0.25), kept only if its name matches endocytosis/trafficking keywords. The x-axis is −log10(FDR) and bubble size grows with term size. The terms are significant (FDR between about 10^-1.5 and 10^-3.2) but much weaker than in the up-regulated list. The input p-values are spot-level and pseudoreplicated.
figs/c841798795a77da1.jpg: **Endocytosis and vesicle-transport GO terms are strongly enriched among genes higher in PBS than WT.** Each bubble is a GO Biological Process term from g:Profiler over-representation analysis of genes up in PBS vs WT (spot-level t-test, FDR ≤ 0.05, log2FC ≥ 0.25), filtered to endocytosis/trafficking keywords. The x-axis is −log10(FDR) and bubble size grows with term size. Vesicle-mediated transport and endocytosis lead (−log10 FDR about 14), followed by lysosome and autophagosome terms. Unlike the gseapy prerank in §13, which found no endocytosis term at FDR < 0.3, this list-based test is driven by spot-level p-values and many genes.
figs/dcd6e272ca451651.jpg: **Genes lower in BRICHOS than WT are enriched for synaptic-vesicle GO terms.** Each bubble is a GO Biological Process term from g:Profiler over-representation analysis of genes down in BRICHOS vs WT (spot-level t-test, FDR ≤ 0.05, log2FC ≤ −0.25), filtered to endocytosis/trafficking keywords. The x-axis is −log10(FDR) and bubble size grows with term size. The terms are about synaptic-vesicle cycling and fusion, with modest significance (−log10 FDR up to about 2.6). The code comment says 'PBS vs WT', but the contrast used is BRICHOS vs WT.
figs/f8d83aeee891d28a.jpg: **Genes higher in BRICHOS than WT show the same endocytosis enrichment as in PBS.** Each bubble is a GO Biological Process term from g:Profiler over-representation analysis of genes up in BRICHOS vs WT (spot-level t-test, FDR ≤ 0.05, log2FC ≥ 0.25), filtered to endocytosis/trafficking keywords. The x-axis is −log10(FDR) and bubble size grows with term size. Endocytosis and vesicle-mediated transport lead (−log10 FDR about 12–16), as in PBS vs WT. The disease-associated endocytic up-shift is therefore not removed by BRICHOS.
figs/2d252a43f1a86a34.jpg: **The 500 most-changed genes in PBS vs WT are enriched for immune and defence GO terms.** Each bubble is one of the 15 most significant GO Biological Process terms from g:Profiler, run on the top 500 genes by |log2FC| among spot-level PBS-vs-WT DE genes (FDR ≤ 0.05), with up and down genes pooled. The x-axis is −log10(FDR) and bubble size grows with term size. Immune system process and immune response lead (−log10 FDR about 15).
figs/924096f691ac8b4d.jpg: **The 500 most-changed genes in BRICHOS vs WT are enriched for immune and stimulus-response GO terms.** Each bubble is one of the 15 most significant GO Biological Process terms from g:Profiler, run on the top 500 genes by |log2FC| among spot-level BRICHOS-vs-WT DE genes (FDR ≤ 0.05), with up and down genes pooled. The x-axis is −log10(FDR) and bubble size grows with term size. The terms are much like PBS vs WT (immune, defence and response to external stimulus), with even higher significance (−log10 FDR about 32–44).
figs/b2bcc773a6c3b782.jpg: **The 500 most-changed genes in BRICHOS vs PBS give only weak, generic GO terms.** Each bubble is one of the 15 most significant GO Biological Process terms from g:Profiler, run on the top 500 genes by |log2FC| among spot-level BRICHOS-vs-PBS DE genes (FDR ≤ 0.05), with up and down genes pooled. The x-axis is −log10(FDR) and bubble size grows with term size. The terms are broad development and immune terms with −log10 FDR only about 3.6–5. Per §13, the top BRICHOS-vs-PBS genes are hypothalamic neuropeptides (Pmch, Hcrt), which point to differences in cutting plane rather than treatment.
figs/b4c48801babb9764.jpg: **The spot UMAP coloured by region, treatment and Leiden-0.3 cluster, as input for pseudobulking.** Each point is a Visium spot from all 10 sections. Top: the ten cluster-derived regions. Middle: treatment group. Bottom: Leiden-0.3 cluster. figs/50742bdb511156a6.jpg: **The top principal components of section × cluster pseudobulks track cluster and region, not treatment.** Bottom heatmap: scores on PC1–PC5 (columns) for each pseudobulk profile (rows), with colour bars on the right for cluster, number of spots, counts, region, section and treatment. Cluster and region are significant on all five PCs and spot/count numbers on PC1–3, while treatment and section are not significant on any. A block of rows with extreme PC1 scores has near-zero spot counts, matching the empty cluster × section profiles noted in §14.
figs/ea57ca2f8d634e05.jpg: **PC1 dominates the variance of the section × cluster pseudobulk profiles.** The plot shows the fraction of variance explained (y) by each of the first 30 principal components, ranked (x). PC1 explains about 40 % and PC2 under 10 %; the rest are small. Given the obsm panel, PC1 is largely driven by a group of near-empty pseudobulk profiles, not by biology.
figs/7d845acaac081334.jpg: **Pseudobulk PCA separates profiles by region; treatment and section do not form groups.** Each point is one section × Leiden-0.3 cluster pseudobulk, plotted on PC1 vs PC2 and coloured by treatment (top), section (middle) and region (bottom). Ventricular-area profiles form a separate group high on PC2, and a stack of overlapping points sits at the far left of PC1. Treatments are interleaved within each region group, so cluster identity, not treatment, drives the main variation.
figs/111c4a2ed9c35569.jpg: **Expression-filter diagnostic for the pseudobulk genes (no filter was actually applied).** Each bin is a group of genes, placed by log10 total counts across pseudobulk profiles (x) and the number of profiles in which the gene passes the minimum count (y); colour is the number of genes. The dashed lines mark the `filter_by_expr` thresholds. A large group of genes sits at the bottom left with very few counts. figs/51f1bfd364054c6f.jpg: **Proportion-filter diagnostic for the pseudobulk genes (no filter was actually applied).** The histogram shows how many genes (y, log scale) are detected above the minimum proportion in a given number of pseudobulk profiles (x). The dashed line marks the `min_smpls = 2` threshold. The distribution is U-shaped: thousands of genes are detected in almost no profiles, and many in nearly all. This is a plot only; the filter was not applied, so low-count genes stayed in the DESeq2 model.
figs/af9eb45d855cb166.jpg: **The pseudobulk PBS-vs-WT volcano is dominated by an arc of implausibly large up-regulated fold changes.** Each point is a gene from pydeseq2 on section × cluster pseudobulks (PBS vs WT); x is log2 fold change and y is −log10 raw p-value. Red marks up and blue down past the dashed thresholds; the top 20 genes are labelled. Cst7, Ccl6, Ccl3 and Cd52 stand out as expected DAM genes. But thousands of genes form a smooth arc with log2FC of 4–9.5, including olfactory and vomeronasal receptors (Vmn2r114, Olfr). This pattern fits the unfiltered low-count genes and non-converged size factors noted in §14, and few genes are called down.
figs/5295c211ce68e3de.jpg: **Transcription-factor activity inferred for PBS vs WT: Hnf1a, Spi1, Nfkb1 and C/EBP factors score highest.** Each bar is one of the top 50 transcription factors by absolute ULM score from CollecTRI targets, scored against the pseudobulk PBS-vs-WT Wald statistic. Positive (red) means target genes are up in PBS. Most factors are positive, led by Hnf1a, Spi1 (PU.1, a microglial factor), Nfkb1 and Hnf1b, with several C/EBP factors. Only four are negative (E2f4, Ppard, Trp53, Myc). Liver/gut factors such as Hnf1a, Hnf4a and Cdx2 scoring high suggests the score is inflated by the skewed statistic (see the volcano).
figs/b6a5a3612e3c6b33.jpg: **Target networks of seven selected transcription factors for PBS vs WT.** Squares are transcription factors, coloured by ULM enrichment score; circles are their top 5 CollecTRI targets, coloured by the PBS-vs-WT statistic; green arrows are activating and red repressing edges. Only four of the seven requested factors are drawn (Myc, Stat3, Stat1, Hnf1a). Their targets are almost all strongly up (yellow), and include non-brain genes such as Hbb-bs, Tshb, Il17f, Cdh17 and Nr1i2, which fits the low-count artefacts in this model.
figs/b4d491c2701b1430.jpg: **The CollecTRI targets of Stat1 are almost all up in PBS vs WT.** Each point is a Stat1 target gene; x is the PBS-vs-WT log2 fold change and y is −log10 raw p-value from the pseudobulk model, with the 10 top genes labelled. Ccl3 and Cxcl9 are plausible inflammatory hits. Many targets lie on the same high-LFC arc (log2FC 6–9.4) seen in the whole-gene volcano, including Tshb, Il21 and Cfhr2, so the Stat1 score is partly driven by artefactual low-count genes.
figs/a4f682dbd38a621f.jpg: **PROGENy pathway activity for PBS vs WT: NF-κB is highest, VEGF lowest.** Each bar is a PROGENy pathway's ULM score against the pseudobulk PBS-vs-WT statistic; red is activated and blue suppressed in PBS. NFkB scores highest (+17.35), followed by Hypoxia, p53 and TNFa (about +12); VEGF (−5.66), PI3K and TGFb are negative. Pseudobulks are section × cluster profiles with one WT section, so the significance is pseudoreplicated.
figs/a51e8f79663864bd.jpg: **PROGENy pathway scores for PBS vs WT, with significance as dot size.** Each dot is a pathway; x and colour are the ULM score, and dot size is −log10 p-value clipped at p = 2.22e-4. The order matches the bar plot, with NF-κB highest and VEGF lowest. The sizes barely differ (legend 3.0–3.5), because most p-values hit the clipping floor.
figs/83ac17e28e8cb3ba.jpg: **How individual MAPK pathway genes contribute to the PBS-vs-WT score.** Each point is a PROGENy MAPK footprint gene; x is its pathway weight and y its PBS-vs-WT Wald statistic. Red points add to pathway activation (weight and statistic have the same sign) and blue points oppose it; the 15 largest contributors are labelled. Classic MAPK feedback genes with large positive weights are up in PBS (Dusp6, Spry2, Fosl1, Egr2), but most genes sit near zero weight. The cloud is skewed to positive statistics.
figs/e74a2ae0ba497cad.jpg: **Running enrichment of one sign of the MAPK footprint along the PBS-vs-WT ranking.** The top panel shows the running enrichment score along genes ranked by the PBS-vs-WT Wald statistic (x, about 18,750 genes); the green ticks are the pathway genes and the bottom panel is the ranked statistic. The cell plots the positive-weight and the negative-weight MAPK genes separately; this image is one of the two, and the two look almost identical. The peak is small (about 0.17) and lies mid-ranking. The ticks cover nearly every gene, so the set is not a specific gene set. Most statistics are positive (the zero crossing is near rank 16,700), which reflects the skewed model.
figs/ef574609599cbaab.jpg: **Running enrichment of the other sign of the MAPK footprint along the PBS-vs-WT ranking.** The panels are as in the companion plot: running enrichment score (top), the positions of the pathway genes (green ticks) and the ranked PBS-vs-WT statistic (bottom). This is the second of the positive-weight/negative-weight pair from the same cell; it peaks at about 0.17 near the middle of the ranking. Both signs give near-identical curves, because the ticks span almost every gene.
figs/97b8369d7823a248.jpg: **Hallmark gene-set activity for PBS vs WT: immune sets up, oxidative phosphorylation and MYC targets down.** Each bar is an MSigDB Hallmark set's ULM score against the pseudobulk PBS-vs-WT statistic; red is higher and blue lower in PBS. Allograft rejection, coagulation, inflammatory response and interferon-γ response are positive. Oxidative phosphorylation (−10.45) and MYC targets V1 are the most negative, followed by DNA repair, mTORC1 signalling and protein secretion.
figs/bcd74d79a54b99dc.jpg: **The ten most significant Hallmark sets for PBS vs WT.** Each dot is a Hallmark set; x and colour are the ULM score, and dot size is meant to show significance. Oxidative phosphorylation and MYC targets V1 are the most negative and most significant; allograft rejection and coagulation are the only positive sets shown. The code sizes dots by log10 of the raw p-value (without the minus sign), so the size legend ('padj' 8 and 12) is not a correct scale.
figs/21282dc75b151fb5.jpg: **Running enrichment of the Hallmark hypoxia set along the PBS-vs-WT ranking.** The top panel shows the running enrichment score along genes ranked by the pseudobulk PBS-vs-WT Wald statistic (x); green ticks mark hypoxia genes; the bottom panel is the ranked statistic. The curve peaks at about 0.3 near rank 9,000, so the leading edge is a broad set of moderately up-ranked genes. Most of the ranking is positive (zero crossing near rank 16,700), which reflects the skewed statistic in this model.
figs/7fbd0aaf337ccd1e.jpg: **The UMAP of WT and BRICHOS spots coloured by region, treatment and Leiden-0.3 cluster.** Each point is a Visium spot from the four WT and BRICHOS sections. figs/6575d23bfbab1d2e.jpg: **WT + BRICHOS pseudobulk PCA groups profiles by region, not treatment.** Each point is one section × Leiden-0.3 pseudobulk, plotted on PC1 vs PC2 and coloured by treatment (top), section (middle) and region (bottom). figs/005fec0468d0a367.jpg: **Expression-filter diagnostic for the WT + BRICHOS pseudobulks (no filter was actually applied).** Each bin is a group of genes, placed by log10 total counts (x) and the number of pseudobulk profiles passing the minimum count (y, up to about 41); colour is the number of genes. figs/68528dc4cf52f1f0.jpg: **Proportion-filter diagnostic for the WT + BRICHOS pseudobulks (no filter was actually applied).** The histogram shows the number of genes (y, log scale) detected above the minimum proportion in a given number of profiles (x). The under-trained reference means the cell-type signatures were not fully fitted, which may contribute to the large noise term and differences from cell2location.
figs/a4ebc32c24c31d51.jpg: **Figure not interpretable.** Intended as per-spot stereoscope MYE:Microglia proportion maps for the six PBS sections, but the spots are drawn too small for any colour to be visible over the H&E images and no colour bar is shown.
figs/b7b52a1ec68731b5.jpg: **Stereoscope microglia by region: WT lowest in most regions, BRICHOS usually between WT and PBS.** Grouped bars give the mean per-spot stereoscope microglia fraction per region for WT (purple), PBS (orange) and BRICHOS (green), pooled over spots. The PBS–BRICHOS gap is largest in cortex, olfactory areas, meninges and caudoputamen, but BRICHOS equals or exceeds PBS in hippocampal formation, hypothalamus, thalamus and ventricular area. Spot-pooled means; the treatment groups are confounded with slide.
figs/1cf11b372d7e2e88.jpg: **Both methods put WT and one P24215 BRICHOS section low, and BRICHOS 401 within the PBS range.** Each point is a section: x = mean microglia fraction from cell2location, y = mean from stereoscope; colour = treatment, circle = slide P28052, triangle = slide P24215. The section-level Spearman correlation between methods is 0.503; WT 101 and BRICHOS 301 are lowest under stereoscope, and BRICHOS 401 (P28052) sits among PBS sections. BRICHOS P24215_201 is low under cell2location but not under stereoscope, so the slide pattern is only partly reproduced.
figs/1dcbe16bf31c6254.jpg: **Per-spot microglia agreement between stereoscope and cell2location is only moderate.** Left: hexbin of per-spot microglia fraction, cell2location (x) vs stereoscope (y), colour = log10 spot count, dashed line = identity; r = 0.54, ρ = 0.48, with stereoscope values spread much wider (up to ~0.5) and mostly above the identity line. Right: mean fraction per spot of each type under the two methods; stereoscope gives more microglia, oligos and peripheral glia and fewer neurons and ependymal cells. The two methods agree on where cell types are better than on microglia.
figs/71b9df27fb0ae93a.jpg: **The homeostatic-up microglial state shift reproduces with stereoscope, and fades once slide is modelled under both methods.** Each point is the BRICHOS − PBS effect (in SD units of z-scored per-spot scores) from a mixed model on microglia hotspot spots, for DAMratio, DAM and Homeostatic signatures; blue = hotspots defined by cell2location, orange = by stereoscope, p values printed. Left (random intercept per section): Homeostatic is higher under BRICHOS with both methods (c2l p = 0.026, stereo p = 0.003) and DAMratio lower but not significant. Right (adding a slide fixed effect): all effects shrink toward zero and none is significant (p 0.22–0.72).
figs/51b272a574d7a1dc.jpg: **Region-matched microglia shift: both methods see BRICHOS lower in most regions, carried by the P24215 sections.** Left: each point is a region; x = BRICHOS vs PBS microglia difference as % of the PBS mean under cell2location, y = the same under stereoscope (dotted line = identity). Both are negative for cortex, caudoputamen, olfactory areas and meninges and near zero for corpus callosum and hypothalamus, with stereoscope giving larger percentages. Right: section means over common regions as % of each method's PBS mean (circle = slide P28052, triangle = P24215; bar = group mean); BRICHOS 401 sits at about 101 % under both methods, while 201 and 301 (P24215) are low, so the deficit tracks slide.
figs/21c25dd08fc53994.jpg: **Stereoscope: BRICHOS below PBS in microglia in five of seven regions.** Bars give the BRICHOS − PBS difference in mean microglia fraction, computed from per-section region means (regions need ≥ 2 sections per arm, ≥ 30 spots); green = BRICHOS lower, orange = higher. The largest deficits are caudoputamen (about −0.027), meninges, supragranular layers and olfactory areas; hypothalamus is near zero and corpus callosum slightly positive. Only meninges reaches Mann–Whitney p < 0.05 (p = 0.048), and the shift is carried by the two BRICHOS sections on slide P24215.
figs/6042603f7d2b4cbf.jpg: **Stereoscope microglia proportion map for the WT section (no colour bar).** Each dot is a spot on P24215_101 coloured by its stereoscope microglia fraction; spots are small, so only the brightest stand out. The brightest spots trace a curved band in the hippocampal region and dark spots dominate the cortex on the right side. Without a colour bar the values cannot be read, so only the relative pattern within the section is usable.
figs/a44dd2a5313ea2c0.jpg: **Figure not interpretable.** Intended as stereoscope microglia proportion maps for the six PBS sections, but the panels are small thumbnails with tiny spots, the spot colours cannot be distinguished from the H&E image, and there is no colour bar.
figs/dd6001382fc52670.jpg: **Stereoscope's noise term depends on region, not on slide or treatment.** Left: mean noise share per spot by region, from about 0.04 in ventricular area to about 0.55 in infragranular layers, high also in caudoputamen and supragranular cortex. Right: mean noise share per section (bar colour = treatment; black edge = slide P24215); sections fall into about 0.24 (P24215_201, P28052_102, P28052_103) and about 0.35 (the rest), with no slide or treatment split. Because the noise is removed before renormalising, BRICHOS–PBS differences are stretched in high-noise regions such as caudoputamen and infragranular cortex.
figs/e3d1b19454f7ca8d.jpg: **Figure not interpretable.** Intended as stereoscope microglia proportion maps for the three BRICHOS sections (P24215_301, P28052_401, P24215_201), but the spots are too small to read colours against the H&E image and there is no colour bar, so no spatial pattern or level can be judged.
figs/ee791e9d0674d0e0.jpg: **Per-section view shows the stereoscope microglia deficit comes from the two P24215 BRICHOS sections.** One panel per region; each marker is one section's mean stereoscope microglia fraction (colour = treatment, circle = slide P28052, triangle = P24215, labels = section number, bar = group mean); titles give BRICHOS vs PBS % and Mann–Whitney p. BRICHOS 401 (P28052) sits within or above the PBS range in every region, while 201 and/or 301 (P24215) pull the BRICHOS mean down; WT 101 (P24215) is lowest everywhere. Differences range from −15.7 % (supragranular) to +0.7 % (corpus callosum), with only meninges near p = 0.05.
figs/3c4b2b79b41a2916.jpg: **Untested regional means suggest a lower DAM:homeostatic ratio under BRICHOS in thalamus, olfactory areas and meninges.** Grouped bars give the mean DAM − Homeostatic score of microglia hotspot spots (cell2location microglia z > 1.5) per region for WT (purple), PBS (orange) and BRICHOS (green). BRICHOS is clearly below PBS in thalamus (about 0.54 vs 0.27), olfactory areas and meninges, similar elsewhere and slightly higher in supragranular layers; WT bars are near or below zero and absent in regions with no WT hotspots. These are spot-level means with no statistical test, and the regional interaction was later found not significant.
figs/508e3af1430578d7.jpg: **Microglia-weighted signatures reproduce a lower DAM:homeostatic ratio under BRICHOS, with no significant regional difference.** A: section-level means of Homeostatic, DAM and DAMratio scores, each spot weighted by its microglia fraction (one dot per section; WT purple, PBS orange, BRICHOS green); DAMratio is lower in BRICHOS (MWU p = 0.0238, the 6-vs-3 floor), Homeostatic and DAM do not differ (p = 0.262, 0.381). B: BRICHOS − PBS DAM:homeostatic difference per region in hotspot spots (negative = less inflammatory); six of eight regions are negative, largest in meninges and olfactory areas, but none is significant and the treatment × region interaction p = 0.192. The lower BRICHOS values come mostly from the two P24215 sections, so this remains slide-confounded.
figs/620d89146b852043.jpg: **No single gene differs between BRICHOS and PBS in microglia hotspots.** Volcano of pseudobulk DESeq2 on hotspot spots per section: each point is a gene, x = log2 fold change BRICHOS/PBS, y = −log10 nominal p. All points are grey because no gene passes FDR (best padj 0.18, Ganab); the cloud is roughly symmetric with a slight skew to positive fold changes among the smallest p values. This fits a program-level rather than single-gene effect, and the contrast is confounded with slide.
figs/7406d8c20bf316ae.jpg: **The microglial state effect is stable across hotspot thresholds and abundance adjustment (but not slide-adjusted).** For Homeostatic, DAM and DAMratio, each point is the BRICHOS − PBS mixed-model β (95% CI) at hotspot thresholds z > 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0, unadjusted (blue) and adjusted for microglia fraction (red), with p values printed. Homeostatic is positive at all thresholds (adjusted p 0.0024 and 0.016 at z > 1.0 and 1.5, not at z > 2.0); DAMratio is negative throughout and significant after adjustment at every threshold; DAM never differs. Spot-level models with only 9 sections, and the check does not address the slide confound.
figs/7506bd2341780278.jpg: **Slide, not treatment, explains the apparent drop in microglia abundance.** One point per section: mean microglia z-score (abundance), grouped by treatment and coloured by Visium slide (purple = P24215, green = P28052), bar = group mean. The three P24215 sections are the lowest (WT 101 about −0.72, BRICHOS 201 about −0.44, BRICHOS 301 about −0.05), while BRICHOS 401 on P28052 sits within the PBS range (about +0.32). Because all PBS sections are on P28052 and two of three BRICHOS sections on P24215, treatment and slide cannot be separated.
figs/7f57d6f89fce5cc7.jpg: **DAM:homeostatic ratio maps show no visible treatment pattern across sections.** Each panel is one section (title colour = treatment); each spot is coloured by its DAM − Homeostatic score on a shared diverging scale (−1 to +1). All sections, including WT, are mostly light red (ratio slightly above zero) with scattered darker spots and no obvious regional or treatment difference by eye. Spot-level scores include non-microglial signal, so this map is descriptive only.
figs/e6aeeafae984edff.jpg: **In microglia-enriched spots, BRICHOS has a higher homeostatic score while DAM is unchanged.** Five panels, one per signature (Homeostatic, DAM, DAMratio, Neuroinflammation, Complement), scored in hotspot spots (microglia z > 1.5); violins = spot distributions, dots = section means (WT n = 1, PBS n = 6, BRICHOS n = 3), titles = mixed-model p for BRICHOS vs PBS. Homeostatic is higher in BRICHOS (p = 0.013) and DAMratio slightly lower (p = 0.056); DAM, Neuroinflammation and Complement do not differ (p 0.39–0.72). WT is a single section and descriptive only, and with slide added the homeostatic effect falls to p = 0.30.
figs/0f97bd7e890b5fe4.jpg: **Within sections, the plaque-niche DAM/PIG response is equally strong under BRICHOS; only the oligodendrocyte negative control differs.** Each panel is one signature; each marker is a section's hot-minus-cold contrast (mean score in microglia-hot spots minus cold spots within each section × region, depth-matched), grouped WT / PBS / BRICHOS (circle = slide P28052, triangle = P24215, black edge = BRICHOS 401), bar = group mean; titles give MWU and mixed-model p and 401's rank among P28052 sections. DAM, PIG, MGnD and Complement contrasts are far above WT in both AD groups with no treatment difference (p 0.38–1.0), and 401 ranks 1/7 for DAM, PIG and MGnD. Among the bottom-right negative controls, neg_Oligo is less negative in BRICHOS (MWU p = 0.02, mixed-model p = 0.003), an unexplained failure.
figs/766df4d875cb1d04.jpg: **Cancelling slide by within-section centring keeps the regional rescue ranking but removes significance, and 401 alone shows a different profile.** Rows are the 7 shared regions; markers compare three designs: uncentred (grey circles, original 03/02 analogue), within-section centred (green squares) and within-slide 401 vs P28052 PBS (orange triangles). Left: PIG concordance (fraction of PIG genes moved toward rescue; dotted line 0.5); middle: PIG rescue slope (negative = rescue); right: permutation p of the slope (red line = 0.05). Centring keeps cortex, meninges and olfactory high and corpus callosum and hypothalamus low, but no p falls below 0.05; 401 alone is most "rescued" in corpus callosum and caudoputamen and least in supragranular cortex.
figs/0e073afb240bbc51.jpg: **After slide-removal corrections, the infragranular cortex rescue stays at the permutation floor.** Each marker is a region's rescue-slope permutation p (log scale; 84 relabelings) under one correction method (none, tech, RUVs k1/k2, RUVg k1/k2), for the 52-gene PIG set (left) and the data-driven disease set (right); red dashed line = 0.05, grey dotted line = floor 1/84 ≈ 0.012. With the data set, infragranular layers is at 0.012 under every method; with PIG, infragranular and supragranular reach 0.024 only after RUVg k1. Corpus callosum and hypothalamus stay non-significant under all methods, and two-factor corrections weaken the PIG cortex result.
figs/4a5020e596bfae57.jpg: **PIG rescue concordance and slope by region under each slide-removal method.** Left heatmap: fraction of PIG genes moved toward rescue (numbers in cells; blue = above 0.5, red = below); right heatmap: PIG rescue slope (blue = negative = rescue, red = positive); columns are correction methods, * = permutation p < 0.05 on the slope. Cortex, meninges and olfactory areas stay blue under every method, and only infragranular and supragranular layers under RUVg k1 are marked significant (slopes −0.12 and −0.14); corpus callosum (concordance 0.10–0.13, positive slope) and hypothalamus remain non-responders. Effects shrink with two-factor corrections, so results depend on how much variance is removed.
figs/fa2421de8ac5d1b0.jpg: **A pure slide contrast mimics a rescue slope more strongly than the real treatment comparison.** Each point is one of the PIG genes: x = disease log2FC (PBS − WT), y = log2FC of a contrast from whole-section pseudobulk; red line = least-squares fit. Slide only (P24215 BRICHOS − BRICHOS 401) gives slope −0.098 with 37 % of PIG genes down; treatment only on the same slide (401 − P28052 PBS) gives +0.026 with 67 % down; the original all-BRICHOS − all-PBS gives −0.040 with 60 % down. The rescue-slope statistic is therefore slide-contaminated, and 401's 67 % PIG-down ranks only 2nd of 7 sections on its slide.
